issue_request: FHIR-11065 was a Published/Persuasive CBCC correction for DSTU2 FHIR-core Consent section 6.4.1. It asked to replace the idiosyncratic "Substitute Decision Maker" wording with generic proxy terminology and to use healthcare-consumer/consumer language instead of client.
initial_application: The Jira comment records svn revision 10603, and git commit 362208d37f5ff6d1154327d54817e05dc6c3634a applied the client-to-healthcare-consumer wording in source/consent/consent-introduction.xml. That commit left "Substitute Decision Maker" unchanged; commit 24a94d510247db95964505364d08c0a287198a9b later moved the same paragraph into source/consent/consent-notes.xml with the stale term intact.
additional_context: Consent is active in source/fhir.ini, and source/consent/consent-notes.xml is the active Consent narrative source containing the affected Privacy Consent Directive paragraph. Current source/consent/consent-introduction.xml already uses generic "personal representative" language. A legacy source/contract/consentdirective.profile.xml occurrence was not edited because fhir.ini notes ConsentDirective became Consent and no active fhir.ini/list reference to that profile was found.
reconciliation: Changed source/consent/consent-notes.xml so the paragraph now says a healthcare consumer may delegate authority to a proxy who may act on their behalf.
source_changes: source/consent/consent-notes.xml: Replaced "Substitute Decision Maker" with "proxy" in the active Privacy Consent Directive paragraph.
